subject: Future Tech
title: Gene Drives: Editing the Wild
description: A quick, practical guide to Gene Drives: Editing the Wild.

hook.text: A gene drive forces a genetic trait to spread through an entire wild population in just a few generations.

buildup.text: Normal inheritance gives a gene a 50% chance of passing on. A CRISPR gene drive pushes that to nearly 100%.

discovery.text: Scientists engineered gene drives in mosquitoes that could block malaria transmission, potentially saving millions.

twist.text: Releasing a gene drive is irreversible. Once it spreads, pulling it back from the wild is virtually impossible.

climax.text: No gene drive has been released in the wild yet. The ecological risks are too uncertain and the ethics too unresolved.

punchline.text: Gene drives could save millions or rewrite ecosystems forever.

quiz.question: What makes a gene drive different from normal inheritance?
